title: Spanish political leaders hold final rallies ahead of general election
seoTitle: Spain general election: party leaders hold final rallies
dek: Spanish political party leaders have held their final campaign rallies ahead of the 29 November general election, with polls indicating a close finish between competing coalitions.
happened: On 5 October, Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez announced an early general election after parliament rejected emergency housing proposals, according to WMAL. The campaign occurred amid rising rental prices, economic pressures, and judicial proceedings involving former senior Socialist Party officials, WMAL reported. On 27 November, party leaders held their final campaign events prior to the vote, according to the BBC and El País. Sánchez addressed over 13,000 supporters in Madrid, claiming that a progressive majority was attainable and accusing opponents of relying on lies and insults, according to El País and the BBC. People's Party leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo campaigned in Barcelona and Seville, promising a new political era focused on decency and good governance while criticizing government performance on corruption, national debt, and recent train crashes, the BBC reported. Vox leader Santiago Abascal addressed supporters in Valencia, accusing the government of betraying Spaniards, according to the BBC.

sides.who: Pedro Sánchez and the Socialist Party
sides.says: Sánchez claimed that a progressive majority was "within sight" and urged voters to mobilize for social rights and job protection. He stated that opponents attempted to turn the vote into a referendum against him.

sides.who: Alberto Núñez Feijóo and the People's Party
sides.says: Feijóo promised a new era of "truth, decency and good governance" and accused Sánchez of failing to address key issues including corruption, national debt, immigration, and rail disasters.
Abascal stated that Sánchez's government had "betrayed" Spaniards. The party campaigned on policies including national priority for welfare benefits and remigration for certain foreign residents.

next: Spain will hold its general election on 29 November to determine the composition of its next parliament and government, according to WMAL and the BBC. Under Spanish law, no opinion polls may be published after the Monday preceding the vote, the BBC reported.
summary: Spain is scheduled to hold a general election on 29 November following the early dissolution of parliament in October over rejected housing legislation. Political leaders concluded their official campaigns on 27 November with major rallies across the country. Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez urged voters to support a progressive majority, while conservative People's Party leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo promised a change in governance. Vox leader Santiago Abascal criticized the sitting government's performance on immigration and security. Opinion polls indicate a close outcome between potential governing coalitions.
